items.content: The train shudders into the station with a mechanical groan, exhaling its cargo of bodies onto the narrow platform before swallowing a fresh crowd whole. Inside, shoulders press against strangers' shoulders, and the collective warmth of a hundred sleepless faces fogs the scratched windows. A woman reads without seeing the words; a man grips the overhead bar as though it might save him from something larger than the train's lurching. Everyone sways together in reluctant communion, carried forward by a city that never once asked if they were ready.

items.content: Below, the cities unraveled like scattered embers, each cluster of light a quiet civilization going about its private business, wholly unaware of the dark shape sliding silently overhead. The clouds caught the glow from beneath, turning faintly amber at their edges, as though concealing small fires within. Up here, sealed against the cold and the roar, there was a strange tenderness to it all — the world made small and jeweled and bearable, the way distance always makes things seem.

items.content: The rain arrived just after midnight, tapping at first like a hesitant visitor, then settling into a steady, relentless percussion against the nylon overhead. Inside the tent, the sound became the whole world — a grey, rushing curtain that erased the forest, the trail, everything beyond the small warm circle of a sleeping bag. There was something ancient about it, something that loosened the shoulders and stilled the restless mind. You remembered, dimly, that shelter has always been this simple.
